text:
nina: Quick q — shipping the JS SDK: do we standardize on global fetch in runtime or bundle undici for Node? thinking about ESM/CJS interop, types, and parity for auth/retry behavior.

sam: prefer runtime-detect + adapter. use global fetch when available, fallback to undici in Node. keeps edge small.

maria: +1. but watch out for Node <18 and older bundlers that don't polyfill. also types — TS needs lib: ['DOM'] to type Request/Response.

joel: For auth/retry parity we need a single wrapper layer in SDK that normalizes responses and errors. fetch implementations differ in timeouts and body stream behavior.

alex: Example runtime-detect pattern that worked for other libs: 
```js
let fetchImpl = globalThis.fetch;
if (!fetchImpl) {
  // dynamically import undici only in Node where needed
  const { fetch: undiciFetch } = await import('undici');
  fetchImpl = undiciFetch;
}
const resp = await fetchImpl(url, opts);
```

sam: That dynamic import solves ESM-only undici in modern projects but breaks in CJS consumers unless we provide a CJS build that calls it via `await import()`.

maria: We should ship an ESM-first package and provide a tiny CJS wrapper that re-exports using `module.exports = require('./dist/interop.cjs').default` to avoid surprises.

joel: On retries: undici has a different error shape for DNS failures vs fetch in edge. SDK should map to our RetryableError / NonRetryableError classes so downstream code can expect the same API.

nina: What about types? People hit TS errors if they don't have `lib.dom` — can we bundle our own minimal types for fetch?

alex: Bundling full DOM types is heavy. Simpler: export a tiny d.ts that declares `export type Fetch = typeof fetch;` and document that consumers should enable DOM lib for full types. Also provide `types` entry in package.json.

maria: Another gotcha: keep-alive/agent behavior. undici supports connection pooling; global fetch in Node might not. We should expose a config knob (agent/keepAlive) only active when undici is used, no-ops in edge. Document fallbacks.

sam: For ESM/CJS interop we also need to ensure default imports work. In CJS: `const { default: createClient } = require('redwood-sdk');` is painful. Provide a minimal compat doc and a small example for CommonJS.

joel: Ops note: Cloudflare/Bun/Deno all have fetch — but Bun has different body streaming behavior. Add runtime tests in CI that run a smoke suite under node (with undici), deno, bun, and cloudflare worker (via wrangler or playwright?).

infra-bot: Created ticket RED-3134: "SDK fetch adapter parity + runtime tests" — https://redwood.internal/RED-3134 :eyes:

devex-bot: FYI added a PR template checklist: ensure `tsconfig` docs + runtime-detect example + retry mapping included. :white_check_mark:

nina: Action items: 1) implement adapter + error mapping, 2) dynamic undici import fallback, 3) add runtime CI matrix, 4) add TS guidance in README. I'll draft a short RFC.

sam: I can pick up the adapter implementation. will prototype with the dynamic import pattern and a small test harness.

maria: I'll write the TS section and examples for CJS consumers.

joel: I'll add the retry/error normalization and some unit tests for error shapes.

alex: I'll create a tiny example repo showing usage in Node (undici), Bun, and Cloudflare.

nina: thanks team — trying to keep onboarding friction low for new users. :seedling:
